one_liner: Samsung's embeddable no-JIT JavaScript interpreter (ES2026, Intl, Temporal); about 1.2-1.3x QuickJS speed on ARM64 suites, with lower RSS on large workloads.
what_it_does: A full ECMAScript 2026 engine with a bytecode interpreter only: no JIT and no writable-executable memory, so it can be embedded in iOS App Store apps, TVs, phones and Cortex-M RTOS targets. You embed it as libescargot (static by default, shared optional) through a C++ API (src/api/EscargotPublic.h: Globals, VMInstanceRef, ContextRef, Evaluator, Memory) or an optional Node-API v10 hosting layer; it is not API-compatible with QuickJS, so switching means rewriting the host bindings.
how_it_is_fast: Source is compiled to a register-based bytecode run by a computed-goto (threaded) dispatch loop, with inline caches for property gets and instanceof and shared object-structure transitions (hidden-class style). Memory is managed by a vendored Boehm-Demers-Weiser conservative collector (third_party/GCutil, thread-isolated heaps), with optional 32-bit-in-64-bit pointer compression and code and string compression aimed at keeping RSS low (the project's Software: Practice and Experience 2023 paper covers dynamic code compression). The v5.0.3 release notes list cutting temporary allocations, streaming UTF-8 sources through bounded parser windows and specialising TypedArray indexed access.
when_to_use: You need modern JavaScript (ES2026 with Intl and Temporal) on a device or store where JIT is not allowed or not affordable: iOS apps, Tizen and Android products, embedded Linux, FreeRTOS or NuttX on Cortex-M.

Large or long-running scripts (bundled apps, parsers, compilers) where QuickJS's RSS grows: on the fixed-work ARM64 runs Escargot averaged 85.7 MiB vs 161.4 MiB on Octane and 171.6 MiB vs 375.9 MiB on Web Tooling.
CPU-bound interpreter work where a 1.2-1.3x gain over QuickJS on ARM64 matters and a C++ embedding API (or Node-API addon compatibility) is wanted.
You want lower memory than V8 --jitless: Escargot used less RSS than d8 --jitless on all three suites (SunSpider 14.2 vs 40.7 MiB, Octane 85.7 vs 152.8, Web Tooling 171.6 vs 265.8).
when_not_to_use: Small scripts and tiny footprints: on SunSpider QuickJS averaged 5.3 MiB RSS vs Escargot's 14.2 MiB, and QuickJS has no ICU dependency.
GC-latency-sensitive workloads: Escargot scored less than half of QuickJS on Octane Splay (1147 vs 2353) and SplayLatency (1872 vs 5405); its collector is a conservative, non-moving bdwgc.

Untrusted or hostile scripts: the README says the project assumes valid JavaScript only, and 2026 reports include a type confusion in InterpreterSlowPath::initializeClassOperation, heap-buffer-overflows and an ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer TOCTOU null dereference.
Peak speed: V8 d8 --jitless (also no JIT) beat it on all three suites (SunSpider 694.6 vs 823.2 ms, Octane 2300 vs 2198, Web Tooling 2.02 vs 1.07 runs/s), and full V8 is about 11x on Octane.
Proprietary products that cannot meet LGPL-2.1 obligations: the default artefact is a static library, so static linking requires providing relinkable objects.

integration.form: static lib (libescargot.a by default; shared library with ESCARGOT_BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON), built with CMake
integration.dependencies: vendored bdwgc (third_party/GCutil submodule); ICU for Intl/Temporal (system ICU via dlopen on Linux, vendored ICU on macOS/iOS, vcpkg or Windows ICU on Windows, or disabled); optional vendored WABT for WebAssembly; Python 3 at build time
integration.min_toolchain: CMake 2.8.12+; GCC or Clang compiling with -std=c++11 on Linux (C++17 on macOS and MSVC); Visual Studio 2022 (MSVC v143) in the Windows example; exact minimum compiler versions not documented
integration.platforms: Linux x86/x64/arm/aarch64/riscv64, Android, Tizen, macOS x64/arm64, iOS arm64 (simulator run in CI, device build-only), Windows x86/x64/arm64 (no WebAssembly on arm64), FreeRTOS/NuttX on Cortex-M
integration.thread_safety: Globals::initialize once per process, then Globals::initializeThread/finalizeThread on each thread that uses the engine; bdwgc is built with GC_THREAD_ISOLATE so each thread has its own heap; sharing one VM instance across threads is not documented beyond the cross-thread job hooks

gotchas: Harness finding: the Web Tooling headline (1.07 vs 0.89 runs/s geomean, about 1.20x) rests on one subtest, coffeescript, where QuickJS ran at 0.05 runs/s against Escargot's 0.86 and V8 --jitless's 2.77 (confirmed in the run's raw quickjs-web_tooling.log). Without it the geomean ratio is about 1.02x (1.083 vs 1.059, derived from page data), and Escargot loses 7 of 18 Web Tooling subtests (babel, babel-minify, buble, chai, jshint, postcss, prepack).

Measurement depth is thin outside SunSpider: Octane is one scored run, and Web Tooling's minSamples was patched from 20 to 3 by the harness; no variance is reported for either. SunSpider is the mean of 5 fresh processes (Escargot 809-830 ms, QuickJS 979-986 ms).

The dashboard binary is built with -DESCARGOT_TCO=ON, which is off by default, and the Release flags are -O2 -fno-stack-protector -fno-omit-frame-pointer; the compiler version is not recorded. ESCARGOT_SMALL_CONFIG's -Os has a known memory conflict with newer GCC (issue #1480), so it is only applied for GCC 9 and older.

Conservative GC: host objects that hold JS values must be allocated with Memory::gcMalloc (or registered), stack scanning can retain dead objects, and the README asks for vulnerability reports through public issues (issue #1662 asks how to report privately).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Escargot over QuickJS when you need Intl/Temporal and run large scripts where its lower RSS on Octane and Web Tooling matters, and over Hermes when you must run plain JavaScript source rather than precompiled bytecode; pick QuickJS (or MicroQuickJS) for the smallest footprint, MIT licensing and short scripts, and Ant or PrimJS if raw interpreter speed over QuickJS matters more than ICU-backed standards coverage.
verified_claims_summary: Escargot's own monthly CI dashboard (2026-10-04, commit fc608b59b, CMake Release -O2 with TCO on) against QuickJS 2026-06-04 built with its Makefile, on one pinned core of an AWS Neoverse-N1 (Arm part 0xd0c) aarch64 host with a shared glibc 2.39 runtime: SunSpider 823.2 vs 981.6 ms (wins 21 of 26 tests), Octane 2198 vs 1689 (wins 15 of 17 sub-scores, loses Splay and SplayLatency), Web Tooling 1.07 vs 0.89 runs/s (about 1.02x without the coffeescript outlier). Fixed-work memory (median of 3 processes) favours Escargot on Octane and Web Tooling and QuickJS on SunSpider.
status_note: Very active (commits through 2026-10-06, release tag v5.0.3, shipped in Samsung Tizen products) and copyable under LGPL-2.1, but treat it as a trusted-code engine: fuzzing reports of memory-safety bugs were still arriving in mid-2026.
